articles.title: Testing AI Agent Guardrails Before Production: A Practical Playbook
articles.excerpt: In February 2024, a Canadian tribunal ordered Air Canada to honor a bereavement refund policy that its support chatbot had invented. The airline argued the bot was responsible for its own words. The t…
articles.body: In February 2024, a Canadian tribunal ordered Air Canada to honor a bereavement refund policy that its support chatbot had invented. The airline argued the bot was responsible for its own words. The tribunal disagreed. If your agent can say it, or do it, you own it. The stakes rise once an LLM stops answering questions and starts calling tools: running shell commands, editing files, sending emails, issuing refunds. Agents bypass rules for mundane reasons. The system prompt is a suggestion, not a permission system. Tool outputs can carry injected instructions. Models also optimize hard toward task completion. You cannot prompt your way out of this. You have to test for it and enforce boundaries outside the model.
articles.author: lucanu

articles.title: What Is OSINT, Exactly - A Builder's Definition That Survives a Legal Review
articles.excerpt: Most "OSINT" articles open with a spy anecdote and close with a tool list. The useful definition is drier and it decides what you're allowed to build: OSINT = intelligence produced from publicly avail…
articles.body: Most "OSINT" articles open with a spy anecdote and close with a tool list. The useful definition is drier and it decides what you're allowed to build: OSINT = intelligence produced from publicly available sources, using a documented method. Three parts, and all three matter: Publicly available - you could, as a member of the public, walk up and see it. A public Telegram channel: yes. A leaked database of that channel's private members: no. A friend's screenshot of a private channel: legally grey, methodologically weak. Sources - the material: posts, pages, registers, filings, code commits. Documented method - the part everyone skips. If you can't write down where each fact came from and when, you have a vibe with a citation, not intelligence.

articles.title: How to Merge PowerPoint Files Using Python
articles.excerpt: When several people prepare slides for the same report, each of them submits a separate deck that someone eventually has to stitch into one presentation. The same happens when building training materi…
articles.body: When several people prepare slides for the same report, each of them submits a separate deck that someone eventually has to stitch into one presentation. The same happens when building training material: you pick a few slides from different files and assemble them into a new deck. Copy-pasting slides by hand is error-prone once the page count grows — slides get missed or end up out of order. With Python you can merge an entire presentation into another, assemble selected slides across files, or duplicate slides within a single deck. This article demonstrates these operations using Spire.Presentation for Python. Why Merge Presentations with Python Doing the job in a script has a few concrete advantages: Batch processing : dozens of submitted decks can be merged in order in one run.

articles.title: I built 59 free browser-based dev tools in vanilla JS — here's what I learned
articles.excerpt: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. The main constraint I set for myself:…
articles.body: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. Why vanilla JS? No React, no build step. The main constraint I set for myself: zero dependencies, zero server, zero telemetry . When you paste your JWT token into jwt.io, it goes to their server. When you use an online regex tester, your test strings are logged. I built Antigravity Tools so every operation runs inside your browser, using native APIs. No Node.js backend No npm packages No webpack/vite/parcel No Google Analytics No cookies Everything runs on Web Crypto API , Canvas API , Web Audio API , and IndexedDB — all native to modern browsers.

articles.title: New Tool to Help Clean WP_Options Table
articles.excerpt: Every WordPress developer knows how important it is to optimize websites for better page speed and performance. One of the best ways to accomplish this is by cleaning the WordPress database wp_options…
articles.body: Every WordPress developer knows how important it is to optimize websites for better page speed and performance. One of the best ways to accomplish this is by cleaning the WordPress database wp_options table. The Problem: Database Bloat Plugin data often remains in the options table even after a plugin is deactivated and deleted. Over time, that leftover plugin data causes database bloat, which increases database size and slows down the website. Unused rows set to autoload = yes are particularly harmful because WordPress loads them into server memory on every single page view. When you go to clean it up, though, it's not always clear by the option prefix which plugin the data actually belongs to.

articles.title: WaterSheep: an open-source alternative to Jev
articles.excerpt: TypeSafe's Jev made a simple idea popular: a model that doesn't write text, only makes decisions. You send some state and typed questions, and you get back choices, scores and probabilities your code…
articles.body: TypeSafe's Jev made a simple idea popular: a model that doesn't write text, only makes decisions. You send some state and typed questions, and you get back choices, scores and probabilities your code can act on. Jev itself is closed, and you pay per token. When it launched, I saw everyone hyping it up and thought: I can build an open one. So I did. WaterSheep is an open-source alternative to Jev. It answers the same kinds of questions about any text: noul : yes/no, with the probability of yes choice : one of your options score : a rating scale, with the expected level multi : every option that applies (Jev doesn't have this one) Every answer includes a probability for every option. Already using Jev?

articles.title: I spent the weekend switching 2FA services, and I wouldn’t wish it on my worst enemy
articles.excerpt: I put it off for as long as I could.
articles.body: I would rather wish that I could avoid some tech-adjacent chores forever. I can’t tell you how long I’ve put off cleaning my PC of dust bunnies, or organizing my tech cupboard with a system that doesn’t hinge entirely on broken boxes and serpentine piles of cables. But as I discovered this past month, none of these tasks quite compares to switching to a new two-factor authentication (2FA) service. 2FA, sometimes called MFA (multi-factor authentication), is one of the many pillars of my online security strategy. It works by issuing a time-based one-time code (TOTP) that serves as a secondary proof of identity when logging in to a service. If 2FA is enabled on a service and you don’t have a 2FA code to go with it, any sign-in attempt will fail.

articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars.

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.

articles.title: Cosmic House of Mirrors
articles.excerpt: Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy clu…
articles.body: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies bunched together on one side of the image, however, are not actually part of the cluster, but rather galaxies much farther away whose light has been bent and magnified by gravitational lensing. This phenomenon occurs when the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Learn more about this galaxy cluster. Image credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 9… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Stickney Crater Explanation: Stickney Crater, the largest crater on the martian moon Phobos, is named for Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall, mathematician and wife of astronomer Asaph Hall. Asaph Hall discovered both the Red Planet’s moons in 1877. Over 9 kilometers across, Stickney is nearly half the diameter of Phobos itself, so large that the impact that blasted out the crater likely came close to shattering the tiny moon.
